sources.title: Operation Dream Job Widespread North Korean Espionage Campaign

claims.value: MITRE describes Lazarus Group as a North Korean state-sponsored group attributed to the Reconnaissance General Bureau; public labels overlap and are not interchangeable without qualification.
MITRE records Operation Dream Job first seen in September 2019 and last seen in August 2020.
ClearSky reported fictitious job offers, reconnaissance, fake LinkedIn profiles, personal-email outreach, and malicious PDF/DOTM/DOC delivery scenarios.
CISA reports trojanized cryptocurrency applications distributed through legitimate-looking sites, phishing, social networking, and social engineering.
claims.source_location: technical summary and initial access variants

claims.value: Public analysis of a Celas Trade Pro sample reported host information collection, XOR protection, and HTTP submission to a reported server path.
CISA and MITRE report that $81 million was stolen from Bangladesh Bank; a larger attempted transfer was stopped after anomalies were detected.
The DOJ complaint as summarized in public government reporting alleges spear-phishing of bank employees before access to terminals interfacing with SWIFT.
Lazarus, Bluenoroff, APT38, BeagleBoyz, and DPRK labels are not treated as interchangeable; the exact operational personnel remain UNKNOWN in this corpus.
The FBI reported destructive malware, theft of proprietary and personal information, thousands of inoperable computers, network outage, and significant operational disruption.
The FBI assessed on December 19, 2014 that the North Korean government was responsible; MITRE and Treasury later linked the operation to Lazarus with explicit attribution caveats.
Public DOJ reporting states that malware was sent to SPE employees; the exact delivery artifact and complete initial-access chain remain UNKNOWN here.

campaigns.name: Operation Dream Job
campaigns.initial_access: Fake job lures and malicious documents; documented scenarios vary by report.
campaigns.execution: Macro and script execution reported in selected cases
campaigns.defense_evasion: Template injection and decoy documents in selected reporting
campaigns.discovery: Active Directory and environment exploration reported in selected cases
campaigns.collection: Information collection reported; complete scope UNKNOWN
campaigns.command_and_control: HTTP(S) and cloud-hosted delivery reported in selected cases
campaigns.exfiltration: Archive and upload behavior reported in selected cases
campaigns.impact: Espionage; one unsuccessful BEC attempt reported
counter_evidence: Exact campaign boundaries among Dream Job, North Star, and Interception are not established.
alternative_hypotheses: Overlapping public labels may represent related but non-identical activity.

campaigns.name: Operation AppleJeus
campaigns.objective: Cryptocurrency theft and access to cryptocurrency-related organizations
campaigns.initial_access: Trojanized cryptocurrency applications, phishing, and social engineering
campaigns.persistence: Hidden updater; exact persistence varies by platform
campaigns.defense_evasion: Valid-looking application and code-signing presentation reported in selected cases
campaigns.discovery: Host identifier, process list, and OS information reported in a sample
campaigns.command_and_control: HTTP C2 reported in selected sample
campaigns.impact: Potential cryptocurrency theft; total impact UNKNOWN
detection: Monitor unsigned or suspicious cryptocurrency applications
Host and HTTP telemetry for updater behavior
forensics: Installer, updater, process, and network artifacts
counter_evidence: The reviewed public sources do not establish one continuous operation for every AppleJeus-named sample.
alternative_hypotheses: Some samples may belong to related but distinct activity sets.

campaigns.name: Bangladesh Bank heist
campaigns.initial_access: Spear-phishing alleged in the DOJ complaint summary
campaigns.defense_evasion: Destruction or manipulation at group level is not promoted to incident fact
campaigns.impact: $81 million reported stolen; larger attempted transfer stopped
campaigns.exploitation_concept: SWIFT transaction manipulation concept; incident-specific implementation UNKNOWN
forensics: SWIFT message and endpoint audit trails
counter_evidence: Exact malware, credential path, and lateral movement are not established in the reviewed sources.
alternative_hypotheses: Group labels overlap and should not be treated as identical.

campaigns.name: Sony Pictures Entertainment intrusion
campaigns.objective: Destructive disruption, theft, and coercive public threats
campaigns.initial_access: Malware sent to employees is reported; exact delivery chain UNKNOWN
campaigns.collection: Proprietary information, PII, and confidential communications reported stolen
campaigns.exfiltration: Data theft reported; exact path UNKNOWN
campaigns.impact: Destructive malware, thousands of inoperable computers, network outage, and business disruption
malware: Destructive wiper; exact family representation is source-dependent
detection: Endpoint destruction and network outage indicators
forensics: Wiper artifacts, compromised accounts, and affected workstation evidence
counter_evidence: Operation-level attribution remains qualified by MITRE's umbrella-term caveat.
alternative_hypotheses: Malware and infrastructure overlap supports linkage but does not identify every operator.
